highlights:
# The lowest published H100 price across the nine providers we track changed hands this week, and it went up. Crusoe listed $3.90 per GPU-hour on September 27 and was not the lowest … | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-10-06T00:00:00+00:00

...

The lowest published H100 price across the nine providers we track changed hands this week, and it went up. Crusoe listed $3.90 per GPU-hour on September 27 and was not the lowest of those nine. Crusoe listed $3.90 on October 4 and was. It never moved its price. Nebius raised past it, so the floor rose five cents and a different company now sets it.

Underneath the published side, the Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones, read A100 80 GB SXM4 at $0.88 on October 4, the lowest weekly reading we have recorded since tracking began on May 18.

H200 is the one you should examine. No provider changed an H200 price this week, and the distance between the lowest published rate across those nine and the traded index still more than doubled, from $0.55 on September 28 to $1.28. Watching list prices alone would have shown you nothing. If you picked a provider on price, the number is not what changed. The name under it is.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
**Bobby Clay**.

...

Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

The full issue, with every provider's lowest observed price and the method notes, is here:
https://lnkd.in/efqfwQWm

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: CoreWeave Alternatives: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Lambda or Crusoe?
results.author: RottenWiFi Team
highlights:
Lambda and Crusoe have the lowest clearly published self-serve H100 rates in the figures captured on October 18, 2026: Lambda lists $3.99 per GPU-hour and Crusoe $4.50. CoreWeave’s North American eight-GPU H100 host is $49.24 per hour (about $6.16 per GPU-hour before accounting for its bundled CPUs, memory, storage and networking). AWS, Azure and Google Cloud can still be the better choice when regional capacity, compliance, distributed-training networks, discounts or an existing data platform matter more than the headline GPU rate.

...

## Crusoe: clear on-demand, spot and network terms

Crusoe lists on-demand B200 at $8.50/GPU-hour, H200 at $5.40, H100 at $4.50 and A100 at $2.30. Its on-demand option is billed hourly or per second, has no minimum commitment and is intended for workloads where uptime and predictable capacity matter. Crusoe also offers spot capacity for jobs that can be stopped and restarted.

results.title: GPU Cloud Prices October 2026: H100, A100, L40S Across 16 Providers
results.author: Bo Shen
highlights:
We collected on-demand GPU list prices from 16 cloud providers three times a day from October 7 to 19, 2026. List prices barely moved: 14 of 407 tracked offers changed. The spread between providers is the real story: H100 from $2.99 to $13.98 per GPU-hour (4.7×), A100 2.6×, L40S 2.1×. And 13 of 22 H100 listings didn't say whether the card is SXM, PCIe or NVL, a difference worth 2.25× in served tokens in our tests.

...

Since October 7 we've collected on-demand GPU list prices three times a day: 42 snapshots so far, about 370 offers from 16 providers. Sources: the Lambda, DigitalOcean and Vultr APIs, and NVIDIA Brev's public catalog, which covers AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Nebius, Crusoe, Hyperstack, Massed Compute and others. The live table is on our GPU prices page. This is the first look at what twelve days of it show; the full October index follows on November 1.

## List prices barely moved

Of 407 offers we tracked across the period, 14 changed price at all:

- One real on-demand cut: an 8×A100 offer from Excess Supply dropped from $3.60 to $1.62 per GPU-hour on October 10 (−55%).
- Back and forth: Google Cloud's 8×H100 alternated between $12.41 and $13.98 per GPU-hour, and its T4 offers moved by about 1%. This looks like the catalog reporting different regions on different days rather than price changes.
- Spot prices moved more: DigitalOcean's spot price for AMD MI355X rose from $2.97 to $5.50 per GPU-hour (+85%), MI350X from $2.46 to $3.50 (+42%), and NVIDIA B300 fell from $8.00 to $6.17 (−23%).

On-demand list prices behave like price lists, not markets: they change in steps, rarely. Whatever is moving in GPU pricing week to week (availability, spot and marketplace prices, negotiated discounts) doesn't show up in the list.

...

The same GPU model costs very different amounts depending on the provider. Taking each provider's cheapest on-demand offer per GPU-hour on October 19:

| GPU | Providers | Cheapest | Median | Most expensive | Spread |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 11 | $2.99 (Vultr) | $3.56 | $13.98 (Google Cloud) | 4.7× |
| A100 | 10 | $1.62 (Hyperstack, Massed Compute, Excess Supply) | $1.98 | $4.18 (Google Cloud) | 2.6× |
| L40S | 9 | $1.06 (Massed Compute) | $1.86 | $2.23 (AWS) | 2.1× |
| H200 | 3 | $4.47 (DigitalOcean) | $4.80 | $6.48 (Nebius) | 1.4× |
| AMD MI300X | 2 | $2.59 (DigitalOcean) | $3.29 | $3.99 (Vultr) | 1.5× |

The big clouds sit at the top of each range. Most of the market clusters well below them: eight of eleven H100 providers list between $2.99 and $4.41.

...

These are list prices at collection time for on-demand capacity. They exclude storage, egress, reserved and committed-use discounts, and they don't tell you whether capacity is available: most offers in the catalog carry no availability flag. Brev's catalog reports one region per offer, which can change between snapshots. Twelve days is a short window. RunPod and peer-to-peer marketplaces where hosts set their own prices aren't included.

results.title: The H100 price is now $5.04 per GPU-hour - Autoresearch - Autoresearch
highlights:
### We tell you when we cancel a price increase

You say to your agent

> “Is the H100 price increase that you announced still on?”

If we cancel a price increase that we announced, the dashboard shows a notice that says so. Each organization that got the email about the increase gets a second email that cancels it. The email includes the text of the first one. See Rates.

...

## October 13, 2026

1. 20:00 UTC

### We tell you about a price increase before it takes effect

You say to your agent

> “Is the price of an H100 going to change soon?”

A price increase now always comes at least 24 hours before it takes effect, and we tell you about it. An increase is a higher list price, or a smaller Friday, weekend, or batch job discount.

When we schedule an increase, the dashboard shows a notice until a few days after it takes effect. The admins and billing members of each organization that used that type in the last 90 days get an email.

Your agent sees it too. Until the increase takes effect, `create_node` and `get_node` carry it in `rate.upcoming_increase`, and `submit_job` carries it in `upcoming_increase`. The field gives the time it takes effect, the new list rate per GPU and per node, and the new discounts. A running node also gets a `price_change` event on `/v1/events`. See Rates.

...

## October 8, 2026

1. 07:00 UTC

### The H100 price is now $5.04 per GPU-hour

On October 8 at 00:00 Pacific time, the H100 list price changed from $3.96 to $5.04 per GPU-hour. Per GPU-minute, the price changed from $0.066 to $0.084. A whole 8-GPU node now costs $40.32 per hour.

The new price applies to each minute that we bill from that time. This includes the minutes of nodes and jobs that were already running. Minutes before that time bill at the old price.

The discounts did not change, and they now apply to the new list price. Friday hours are 33% off, and Saturday and Sunday hours are 20% off, on the Pacific calendar. Batch jobs are 25% off the list price. The docs show the rates.

We did not tell you about this change before it took effect. We are sorry for the late notice. If you have a question about your bill, send it to us on the contact page.
